arxiv-2103-01780.title: A Region-Based Descriptor Network For Uniformly Sampled KeyPoints
arxiv-2103-01780.creator: Kai Lv, Zongqing Lu, Qingmin Liao
arxiv-2103-01780.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kai Lv, Zongqing Lu, Qingmin Liao. Matching keypoint pairs of different images is a basic task of computer vision. Most methods require customized extremum point schemes to obtain the coordinates of feature points with high confidence, which often need complex algorithmic design or a network with higher training difficulty and also ignore the possibility that flat regions can be used as candidate regions of matching points. In this paper, we design a region-based descriptor by combining the context features of a deep network.

arxiv-2108-08582.title: Influence of charged walls and defects on DC resistivity and dielectric relaxations in Cu-Cl boracite
arxiv-2108-08582.creator: C. Cochard, T. Granzow, C. M. Fernandez-Posada, M. A. Carpenter, R. G. P. McQuaid, J. M. Guy, R. W. Whatmore, J. M. Gregg
arxiv-2108-08582.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C. Cochard, T. Granzow, C. M. Fernandez-Posada, M. A. Carpenter, R. G. P. McQuaid, J. M. Guy, R. W. Whatmore, J. M. Gregg. Charged domain walls form spontaneously in Cu-Cl boracite on cooling through the phase transition. These walls exhibit changed conductivity compared to the bulk and motion consistent with the existence of negative capacitance.

arxiv-2205-07413.title: Thermal super-jogs control high-temperature strength in Nb-Mo-Ta-W alloys
arxiv-2205-07413.creator: Sicong He, Xinran Zhou, Dan Mordehai, Jaime Marian
arxiv-2205-07413.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sicong He, Xinran Zhou, Dan Mordehai, Jaime Marian. Refractory multi-element alloys (RMEA) with body-centered cubic (bcc) structure have been the object of much research over the last decade due to their high potential as candidate materials for high-temperature applications. Most of these alloys display a remarkable strength at temperatures above 1000 ∘ C, which cannot be explained by the standard model of bcc plasticity dominated by thermally-activated screw dislocation motion.

arxiv-2206-08187.title: Approximating optimization problems in graphs with locational uncertainty
arxiv-2206-08187.creator: Marin Bougeret
arxiv-2206-08187.description: Abstract Many combinatorial optimization problems can be formulated as the search for a subgraph that satisfies certain properties and minimizes the total weight. We assume here that the vertices correspond to points in a metric space and can take any position in given uncertainty sets.

arxiv-2206-14775.title: RSA cryptosystem for rings with commuting ideals
arxiv-2206-14775.creator: Nasrutdinov M.F., Tronin S.N
arxiv-2206-14775.description: Abstract . This article presents a generalization of the RSA cryptosystem for rings with commuting ideals. An analogue of the Euler function for ideals and the concept of an RSA-ideal are defined. An analog of a cryptosystem for the ring with commuting ideals is formulated and a description of the RSA-ideals for which this is possible is obtained. 1.

arxiv-2208-06895.title: Thermodynamics of deterministic finite automata operating locally and periodically
arxiv-2208-06895.creator: Thomas E. Ouldridge, David H. Wolpert
arxiv-2208-06895.description: Abstract Real-world computers have operational constraints that cause nonzero entropy production (EP). In particular, almost all real-world computers are “periodic”, iteratively undergoing the same physical process; and “local”, in that subsystems evolve whilst physically decoupled from the rest of the computer.

arxiv-2302-06997.title: Data Release of the AST3-2 Automatic Survey from Dome A, Antarctica 2023 Data Release of the AST3-2 Automatic Survey from Dome A, Antarctica – 4
arxiv-2302-06997.creator: Xu Yang, Yi Hu, Zhaohui Shang, Bin Ma, Michael C.B. Ashley, Xiangqun Cui, Fujia Du, Jianning Fu, Xuefei Gong, Bozhong Gu, Peng Jiang, Xiaoyan Li, Zhengyang Li, Charling Tao, Lifan Wang, Lingzhe Xu, Shi-hai Yang, Ce Yu, Xiangyan Yuan, Ji-lin Zhou, Zhenxi Zhu
arxiv-2302-06997.description: Abstract AST3-2 is the second of the three Antarctic Survey Telescopes, aimed at wide-field time-domain optical astronomy. It is located at Dome A, Antarctica, which is by many measures the best optical astronomy site on the Earth’s surface. Here we present the data from the AST3-2 automatic survey in 2016 and the photometry results.

arxiv-2303-10128.title: Direct and indirect evidence of compression of word lengths. Zipf’s law of abbreviation revisited.
arxiv-2303-10128.description: Abstract Zipf’s law of abbreviation, the tendency of more frequent words to be shorter, is one of the most solid candidates for a linguistic universal, in the sense that it has the potential for being exceptionless or with a number of exceptions that is vanishingly small compared to the number of languages on Earth.

arxiv-2305-04754.title: Is AUC the best measure for practical comparison of anomaly detectors? Journal: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
arxiv-2305-04754.creator: Vít Škvára, Tomáš Pevný, Václav Šmídl
arxiv-2305-04754.description: Abstract The area under receiver operating characteristics (AUC) is the standard measure for comparison of anomaly detectors. Its advantage is in providing a scalar number that allows a natural ordering and is independent on a threshold, which allows to postpone the choice.

arxiv-2310-17543.title: On invariant distributions of Feller Markov chains with applications to dynamical systems with random switching
arxiv-2310-17543.creator: Michel Benaïm, Oliver Tough
arxiv-2310-17543.description: Abstract We introduce simple conditions ensuring that invariant distributions of a Feller Markov chain on a compact Riemannian manifold are absolutely continuous with a lower semi-continuous, continuous or smooth density with respect to the Riemannian measure. This is applied to Markov chains obtained by random composition of maps and to piecewise deterministic Markov processes obtained by random switching between flows.

arxiv-2311-12660.title: Visually Guided Object Grasping Thanks: The work described herein has been supported by the European ESPRIT-III programme through the SECOND project (Esprit-BRA No. 6769).
arxiv-2311-12660.creator: Radu Horaud, Member, IEEE, Fadi Dornaika, Bernard Espiau
arxiv-2311-12660.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Radu Horaud, Member, IEEE, Fadi Dornaika, Bernard Espiau. In this paper we present a visual servoing approach to the problem of object grasping and more generally, to the problem of aligning an end-effector with an object. First we extend the method proposed in [ 1 ] to the case of a camera which is not mounted onto the robot being controlled and we stress the importance of the real-time estimation of the image Jacobian.

arxiv-2405-20409.title: ZTF SN Ia DR2: Peculiar velocities’ impact on the Hubble diagram
arxiv-2405-20409.creator: B. Carreres ,, D. Rosselli ,, J. E. Bautista, F. Feinstein, D. Fouchez, B. Racine, C. Ravoux, B. Sanchez, G. Dimitriadis, A. Goobar, J. Johansson, J. Nordin, M. Rigault, M. Smith, M. Amenouche, M. Aubert, C. Barjou-Delayre, U. Burgaz, W. D’Arcy Kenworthy, T. De Jaeger, S. Dhawan, L. Galbany, M. Gino
arxiv-2405-20409.description: Abstract Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are used to determine the distance-redshift relation and build the Hubble diagram. Neglecting their host-galaxy peculiar velocities (PVs) may bias the measurement of cosmological parameters. The smaller the redshift, the larger the effect is.

arxiv-2409-14679.title: Quantifying Context Bias in Domain Adaptation for Object Detection
arxiv-2409-14679.creator: Hojun Son hojunson@umich.edu, Asma Almutairi asmaalm@umich.edu, Arpan Kusari kusari@umich.edu
arxiv-2409-14679.description: Abstract Domain adaptation for object detection (DAOD) has become essential to counter performance degradation caused by distribution shifts between training and deployment domains. However, a critical factor influencing DAOD—context bias resulting from learned foreground-background (FG–BG) associations—has remained underexplored. In this work, we present the first comprehensive empirical and causal analysis specifically targeting context bias in DAOD.

arxiv-2412-09790.title: Critical threshold for weakly interacting log-correlated focusing Gibbs measures
arxiv-2412-09790.creator: Damiano Greco, Tadahiro Oh, Liying Tao, and Leonardo Tolomeo
arxiv-2412-09790.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Damiano Greco, Tadahiro Oh, Liying Tao, and Leonardo Tolomeo. We study log-correlated Gibbs measures on the d d -dimensional torus with weakly interacting focusing quartic potentials whose coupling constants tend to 0 0 as we remove regularization.

arxiv-2601-12950.title: ImmersiveFlow: Stereo-to-7.1.4 Spatial Audio Generation with Flow Matching
arxiv-2601-12950.creator: Zining Liang, Runbang Wang, Xuzhou Ye, Qiuqiang Kong
arxiv-2601-12950.description: Abstract Immersive spatial audio has become increasingly critical for applications ranging from AR/VR to home entertainment and automotive sound systems. However, existing generative methods remain constrained to low-dimensional formats such as binaural audio and First-Order Ambisonics (FOA). Binaural rendering is inherently limited to headphone playback, while FOA suffers from spatial aliasing and insufficient resolution for high-frequency.

europmc-pmc5516186.title: Pediatric obesity is associated with an altered gut microbiota and discordant shifts in Firmicutes populations.
europmc-pmc5516186.creator: Riva A, Borgo F, Lassandro C, Verduci E, Morace G, Borghi E, Berry D.
europmc-pmc5516186.description: An altered gut microbiota has been linked to obesity in adulthood, although little is known about childhood obesity. europmc-pmc8478580.title: Characterising long COVID: a living systematic review.
europmc-pmc8478580.creator: Michelen M, Manoharan L, Elkheir N, Elkheir N, Cheng V, Dagens A, Hastie C, O'Hara M, Suett J, Dahmash D, Bugaeva P, Rigby I, Munblit D, Harriss E, Burls A, Foote C, Scott J, Carson G, Olliaro P, Sigfrid L, Stavropoulou C.
europmc-pmc8478580.description: Background While it is now apparent clinical sequelae (long COVID) may persist after acute COVID-19, their nature, frequency and aetiology are poorly characterised. This study aims to regularly synthesise evidence on long COVID characteristics, to help inform clinical management

pmc-11310447.title: Analysis and evaluation of Camellia oleifera Abel. Germplasm fruit traits from the high-altitude areas of East Guizhou Province, China
pmc-11310447.creator: Xianqin Wan, Dongchan Sun, Yanmei Nie, Qimei Wang, Tianfeng Zhang, Rui Wang, Feifei Li, Xudong Zhao, Chao Gao
pmc-11310447.description: Camellia oleifera, a significant woody edible oil species, was examined using 48 germplasm resources from high-altitude regions in East Guizhou Province, China, to analyze fruit quality. The analysis aimed to identify high-performance germplasm, providing theoretical and research foundations for selecting and cross-breeding superior C. oleifera varieties in these regions.

pmc-11492888.title: Resveratrol Mitigates Uremic Toxin-Induced Intestinal Barrier Dysfunction in Chronic Kidney Disease by Promoting Mitophagy and Inhibiting Apoptosis Pathways
pmc-11492888.creator: Cai-Mei Zheng, Yi-Chou Hou, Kuo-Wang Tsai, Wan-Chung Hu, Hsiu-Chien Yang, Min-Tser Liao, Kuo-Cheng Lu
pmc-11492888.description: Background: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a systemic progressive disorder related to uremic toxins. Uremic toxins disturb intestinal epithelial destruction and barrier dysfunction leading to gut-renal axis disorders in CKD. We examine the protective role of Resveratrol (RSV) against uremic toxin indoxyl sulphate (IS) related intestinal barrier disturbances among CKD.

pmc-11691348.title: A QUALITATIVE STUDY ON THE EXPERIENCE OF SMART CARE TECHNOLOGY UTILIZATION AMONG OLDER ADULTS IN KOREA
pmc-11691348.creator: Sungwan Kang, Boram Hwang, Haklyoung Kim, Seongsu Choi, Kyoungmi Mun, Yeong Ju Lee
pmc-11691348.description: To address the increasing desire among older adults who live alone to remain in the community, the Korean government and Korean companies have implemented pilot projects aimed at expanding smart technology integrated care services. Evaluations of these efforts have primarily focused on cost savings and the number of emergency rescue cases through the replacement of care personnel.

pmc-12558608.title: Novel insights into neuropathy: The impact of prolonged hyperglycemia on long non-coding RNA expression
pmc-12558608.creator: Kamila Zglejc-Waszak, Jan Paweł Jastrzebski, Joanna Wojtkiewicz, Zenon Pidsudko, Judyta Karolina Juranek, Li Shen, Li Shen, Li Shen
pmc-12558608.description: Multiple evidence suggests that type 1 diabetes triggers perturbations in the nervous system both in human patients as well as in animal models of the disease. These perturbations are likely controlled by the expression of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and are present both in peripheral and central nervous system.

pmc-12567167.title: Broccoli to the Lab: Green-Synthesized N-CQDs for Ultrasensitive “Turn-On” Detection of Norfloxacin in Food
pmc-12567167.creator: Zubair Akram, Anam Arshad, Sajida Noureen, Muhammad Mehdi, Ali Raza, Nan Wang, Feng Yu
pmc-12567167.description: Highlights What are the main findings? A novel broccoli-derived nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots (N-CQDs) was successfully synthesized via a green hydrothermal method, using 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP) as both a nitrogen dopant and functionalizing agent; the N-CQDs have an average diameter of ~4.2 nm and emit bright blue fluorescence (λem = 445 nm under λex = 360 nm).

pmc-12632007.title: Triad of homocysteine, ROCK2 and vimentin as a convergent biomarker signature in pseudoexfoliation
pmc-12632007.creator: Lipsa Sahoo, Pranjya Paramita Mohanty, Debasmita Pankaj Alone
pmc-12632007.description: BackgroundPseudoexfoliation (PEX) is a complex age-related disorder traditionally considered ocular in origin but increasingly recognized as a systemic condition involving extracellular matrix (ECM) dysregulation, oxidative stress, and cytoskeletal alterations. The disease typically presents as pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEXS), with a subset of patients progressing to pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PEXG), characterized by elevated intraocular pressure and optic nerve damage.

pmc-13092868.title: Patterns of weariness-related symptoms in Parkinson’s disease: impact of disease progression and levodopa treatment
pmc-13092868.creator: Danielle Hersonsky, Assaf Benesh, Edmund Ben-Ami, Eitan Raveh
pmc-13092868.description: BackgroundWeariness-related symptoms (WRS), i.e. fatigue, daytime sleepiness, and sleep problems are common non-motor symptoms in Parkinson’s disease (PD) that impair quality of life. Although related, they represent distinct clinical domains, and the role of dopaminergic therapy in their progression remains unclear. We compared stable levodopa regimens with levodopa dose escalation to evaluate their impact on WRS evolution.

pmc-13133725.title: Inequality in Physical Activity in Organized Group Settings for Children: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13133725.creator: Ann E Rogers, Christopher S Wichman, Michaela A Schenkelberg, David A Dzewaltowski
pmc-13133725.description: Background:Adult-led organized settings for children (eg, classrooms) provide opportunities for physical activity (PA). The structure of setting time may influence inequalities (ie, unequalness) in the distribution of PA. This study examined differences in PA inequality by setting and time-segment purpose in time-segmented organized group settings for children.

pmc-13436732.title: Effects of hydrokinesitherapy on balance and walking ability for stroke survivors: update of a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled studies
pmc-13436732.creator: Feiyang LIU, Jianglong LIAO, Zeli ZHAO, Guoyan YANG, Shixian LI, Zhen HAN, Li LI, Guanli XIE

pmc-13474558.creator: Takashi Hongo, Tetsuya Yumoto, Takafumi Obara, Tomohiro Hiraoka, Yoshinori Kosaki, Shunta Jinno, Ippei Matsuo, Misa Sasanami, Yuya Miyoshi, Shodai Yoshihiro, Takahiro Tsuge, Atsunori Nakao, Hiromichi Naito

pmc-13512009.title: Optical Spectroscopy and Spectral Imaging for Bladder Cancer Detection and Characterisation: A Scoping Review of Diagnostic Evidence and Translational Readiness
pmc-13512009.creator: Arthur Vander Stichele, Ben Van Cleynenbreugel
pmc-13512009.description: Background/Objectives: White-light cystoscopy remains central to bladder cancer detection and surveillance, but diagnostic uncertainty persists in detecting flat lesions, particularly carcinoma in situ, distinguishing inflammatory mimics, and targeting biopsies. Optical spectroscopy and spectral imaging may provide objective tissue information beyond visual inspection. This scoping review mapped the diagnostic evidence and translational readiness of these technologies.

pmc-13678880.title: Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies
pmc-13678880.creator: Taegeun Lee, Ye-Rin Kim, Euijin Lee, Sae-Ock Oh
pmc-13678880.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Efficient delivery of plasmid DNA (pDNA) into the nucleus remains a major bottleneck in nonviral gene therapy, particularly in post-mitotic and slowly dividing cells where the nuclear envelope constitutes a permanent barrier to passive entry. This review considers the two main strategies for active nuclear targeting: nuclear localisation signal (NLS) peptides, which recruit importin-α/β receptors directly to DNA cargo, and DNA nuclear targeting sequences (DTS), which exploit NLS-bearing transcription factors to mediate piggyback nuclear import.
